title: Hot Elote Dip
description: A lighter hot elote-style corn dip built around deeply charred corn and a strained corn purée, with cotija, lime, garlic, and smoky chile instead of a heavy mayo base.
ingredients: About 4 cups corn kernels, fresh or thawed frozen
About 1/3 cup water, plus more as needed for blending
1 small garlic clove, finely grated or minced
1/2 cup crumbled cotija, plus more for finishing
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Blend roughly half of the corn with the water until smooth, then press the purée through a fine strainer. The finer the strain, the smoother the finished dip.
Melt the butter in a wide sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the remaining whole corn and cook until well toasted with some dark charred spots.
Add the garlic and cook briefly until fragrant.
Pour in the strained corn purée and reduce until it thickens enough to coat the corn.
Lower the heat and stir in the cotija, mayonnaise, lime zest and juice, chipotle, ancho, black pepper, and salt.
Adjust the texture with a small splash of water if needed. The dip should be creamy and scoopable rather than stiff.
Transfer to a warm serving dish and finish with additional cotija. Serve hot.
notes: This came from the corn cacio y pepe idea: use the corn itself to create most of the creamy body, then keep the mayo restrained so the dip stays corn-forward rather than heavy.
